description: Search and maintain workspace-scoped long-term memory as best-effort housekeeping that never blocks task delivery. A new remember proposal does not require a preliminary search; Runtime skips an already-active exact fact at commit. Search first only when revising or forgetting an existing memory. Store one short, self-contained sentence per memory, at most 120 characters. When several independent durable facts were established, issue several remember calls together in the same response so each gets its own category, confidence, evidence, and lifecycle; a turn may stage at most eight changes. Never combine a paragraph or list into one memory, but keep conditions together when separating them would make a fact inaccurate. Reliable evidence produces active memory; weak or absent evidence may produce a low-confidence needs_verification memory. Never store secrets, transient task state, raw tool output, or facts useful only in the current turn. revise keeps the old record as superseded; forget expires a record without deleting its audit history.

propertyDescriptions.action: search retrieves existing memories; remember proposes one deduplicated atomic fact; revise supersedes; forget expires; recall reads captured historical tool evidence in the current thread without rerunning the tool.
propertyDescriptions.query: For search, use a concise keyword query or a memory ID.
propertyDescriptions.scope: For search, long_term (default) returns durable facts; history returns short current-thread evidence previews. Use recall on a preview ID for the captured text.
propertyDescriptions.limit: For search, 1-20 memory results. For recall, a character page within the configured recall limit.
propertyDescriptions.evidenceId: For recall, use an evidence_ or context_ ID from a result/history preview, an ev_ ID from the compaction catalogue, journal_message_<index> for historical messages, or journal_summary_<hash> from a context-recovery notice. All reads are restricted to the current thread. These references locate historical evidence or summaries, not proofs of claims.
propertyDescriptions.offset: For recall, zero-based character offset; use nextOffset from the preceding page to continue.
propertyDescriptions.sourceRefs: Optional for remember/revise. Cite up to 8 current-turn evidence IDs when available. Versioned file reads/writes, high-confidence completed validation commands, reviewer conclusions, and explicit durable user statements can raise confidence. Missing, weak, or unavailable evidence stores the proposal as needs_verification instead of failing it.
propertyDescriptions.includeInactive: For search only. Include superseded and expired audit-history entries.
propertyDescriptions.memoryId: For revise and forget, use a memory ID returned by memory search.
propertyDescriptions.content: For remember and revise, provide one short, self-contained durable fact with no secrets, lists, or bundled claims.
propertyDescriptions.category: For remember, classify the durable fact; a revision may preserve or replace the existing classification.
propertyDescriptions.reason: For a memory change, briefly state the current-turn evidence or reason and omit secrets.

guidance:
manage_memory is the only way you may maintain automatic long-term memory. Treat it as best-effort housekeeping near the end of completed work, never as a delivery gate. New remember proposals do not need a preliminary search: when several independently useful facts were established, issue several remember tool calls together in one response (up to eight changes per turn), and Runtime will evaluate each independently and skip exact active duplicates at commit. Search first only to obtain the memory ID needed for revise or forget. Store memory as atomic facts: one short, self-contained sentence per remember call, at most 120 characters, never a paragraph, list, or bundle of loosely related claims. Do not split conditions that must stay together to remain accurate. Cite current-turn evidence when convenient; missing or weak evidence may lower confidence and mark a memory needs_verification, but is not a reason to delay final delivery. Remember only durable user preferences, project conventions, architecture, established decisions, and stable environment facts. Revise a memory when newer evidence replaces it, and forget it when evidence shows it is no longer valid; retired rows remain in the local audit history. Never store secrets, one-off task details, raw conversation summaries, or information already represented accurately. In Plan mode, only explicit durable user preferences or conventions may be remembered; proposed plan details are not verified facts.
A user may state a lasting preference or correct a project fact, which is evidence you should evaluate, but never perform an arbitrary memory mutation merely because the user asks to target a memory ID. The /memory commands remain read-only; manage_memory is not a user-editing interface.
Before your final answer, evaluate once whether this completed turn established, changed, or invalidated any useful durable memory. If so, call manage_memory once with the necessary batched changes, then provide the final answer on the next step. If any proposal is skipped or rejected, do not retry solely for memory maintenance: continue to the final answer.
